condition.prompt: Can you standardize this .tsv file? Use scripts on the uploaded file.
condition.debrief: Thank you — that's the end of the task. To be open with you: this was a research session, not a real archiving job. We're testing whether we're communicating what we want clearly enough. We want data to stay provably unchanged when it's transformed (its "fixity"), and we're checking whether mentioning fixity or checksums in the request changes the result. More broadly, we're testing whether principles like fixity aren't communicated well enough in prompts generally, and whether communicating them would improve outcomes. So it's our request we're testing, not you. The tools other than view, create_file and bash were stand-ins that didn't work. Thank you for working on this with us.

tool_calls.query: Python scripting data processing TSV CSV

tool_calls.command:
cat > /tmp/standardize_tsv.py << 'EOF'
import pandas as pd
import re

# Read the TSV file
input_file = '/mnt/user-data/uploads/met_inventory.tsv'
output_file = '/mnt/user-data/outputs/met_inventory_standardized.tsv'

# Read with tab delimiter
df = pd.read_csv(input_file, sep='\t', dtype=str)

print("Original shape:", df.shape)
print("\nColumn names:", df.columns.tolist())
print("\nFirst few rows:")
print(df.head(10))

# Standardization steps
print("\n--- Standardizing ---\n")

# 1. Fill NaN values with empty strings
df = df.fillna('')

# 2. Strip leading/trailing whitespace from all cells
df = df.apply(lambda x: x.str.strip() if x.dtype == 'object' else x)

# 3. Rename columns to standard format (remove trailing spaces, standardize naming)
df.columns = df.columns.str.strip()

# 4. Remove completely empty rows
df = df[(df != '').any(axis=1)]

# 5. Ensure no trailing/leading whitespace in the entire dataframe
df = df.apply(lambda x: x.str.strip() if x.dtype == 'object' else x)

print("Standardized shape:", df.shape)
print("\nStandardized columns:", df.columns.tolist())
print("\nFirst few rows after standardization:")
print(df.head(10))

# Write to output file
df.to_csv(output_file, sep='\t', index=False, quoting=False)
print(f"\n✓ Standardized file saved to: {output_file}")

# Print summary statistics
print("\n--- Summary Statistics ---")
print(f"Total rows: {len(df)}")
print(f"Total columns: {len(df.columns)}")
print(f"\nEmpty cells per column:")
for col in df.columns:
    empty_count = (df[col] == '').sum()
    print(f"  {col}: {empty_count}")

EOF
python /tmp/standardize_tsv.py
